'''Jaden McDaniels''' (born September 29, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]]. He attended [[Federal Way High School]] in [[Federal Way, Washington]], where he was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and Washington [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] as a senior. McDaniels was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2019 class. He is the younger brother of basketball player [[Jalen McDaniels]].

==Early life==
McDaniels played basketball for [[Federal Way High School]] in [[Federal Way, Washington]]. As a freshman, he was teammates with his older brother [[Jalen McDaniels|Jalen]] and helped Federal Way win its second straight Class 4A state championship.<ref name="tj">{{cite web |last1=Cotterill |first1=TJ |title=Federal Way has one of the top basketball recruits in the country – a 6-foot-9 guard |url=https://www-1.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article189918159.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |access-date=July 21, 2019 |date=December 14, 2017 |archive-date=July 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722152800/https://www-1.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article189918159.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> McDaniels averaged 2.4 points and 1.8 rebounds per game on the [[varsity team]] and was forced to shoot with his left hand due to a right elbow injury.<ref name="evans2">{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda |title='The future of basketball' plays at Federal Way High School. His name is Jaden McDaniels. |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/hes-the-future-of-basketball-federal-ways-jaden-mcdaniels-has-become-one-of-the-best-in-nation/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=July 21, 2019 |date=February 20, 2019}}</ref> In his first two years, he helped his team win 63 consecutive games, the longest win streak in state history since 1977.<ref name=tj/>

As a junior, McDaniels guided Federal Way to a runner-up finish at the 4A state tournament.<ref name="evans">{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Jayda |title=Gonzaga Prep rallies past Federal Way for 4A state boys championship |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/gonzaga-prep-rallies-past-federal-way-for-4a-state-boys-championship/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=July 21, 2019 |date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> In the season, he averaged 21.3 points, 10 rebounds, 4.6 assists, and 3.3 blocks per game and earned ''[[USA Today]]'' All-USA Washington first team honors.<ref name="usatoday">{{cite web |title=2017-18 ALL-USA Washington Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-washington-boys-basketball-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=July 21, 2019 |date=April 16, 2018}}</ref> In May 2018, McDaniels saw breakout success at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) with Seattle Rotary, bolstering his position as a top recruit in the 2019 class.<ref name="maxpreps">{{cite web |title=Washington forward Jaden McDaniels is EYBL's biggest spring stock-booster |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/GDZMgvP4SkO90YUVy9IUMw/washington-forward-jaden-mcdaniels-is-eybls-biggest-spring-stock-booster.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=July 21, 2019 |date=May 25, 2018}}</ref><ref name="norlander">{{cite web |last1=Norlander |first1=Matt |title=Jaden McDaniels' dad isn't the next LaVar Ball, but he's controlling his 5-star son's recruitment |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/jaden-mcdaniels-dad-isnt-the-next-lavar-ball-but-hes-controlling-his-5-star-sons-recruitment/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=July 21, 2019 |date=July 17, 2018}}</ref>

On January 25, 2019, as a senior, he recorded 51 points against [[Todd Beamer High School]], breaking the school single-game scoring record held by NBA player [[Donny Marshall]].<ref name="joyce">{{cite web |last1=Joyce |first1=Nathan |title=All-American indeed: Federal Way's Jaden McDaniels breaks school record with 51 |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/all-american-indeed-federal-ways-jaden-mcdaniels-breaks-school-record-with-51/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=July 21, 2019 |date=January 25, 2019}}</ref> McDaniels averaged 23.3 points, 10 rebounds, four assists and two blocks per game in his senior season, leading his team to third place at the 4A state tournament.<ref name="smith">{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Lauren |title=Federal Way's McDaniels has all the numbers – and the talent and drive to go with it |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article227359224.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |access-date=July 21, 2019 |date=March 10, 2019}}</ref> He earned Class 4A Player of the Year and Washington [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] recognition.<ref name="joyce2">{{cite web |last1=Joyce |first1=Nathan |title=Federal Way's Jaden McDaniels named WIBCA Class 4A player of year |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/federal-ways-jaden-mcdaniels-named-wibca-class-4a-player-of-year/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=July 21, 2019 |date=March 7, 2019}}</ref><ref name="gatorade">{{cite web |title=Jaden McDaniels 2018 - Gatorade Player of the Year |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/jaden-mcdaniels/37171 |publisher=[[Gatorade]] |access-date=July 21, 2019 |archive-date=March 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322171451/https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/jaden-mcdaniels/37171 |url-status=dead }}</ref> McDaniels played in the [[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]].<ref name="hammond">{{cite web |last1=Hammond |first1=Andrew |title=Washington commit Stewart, Federal Way's McDaniels stand out at 2019 McDonald's All-American Game |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/article228601659.html |website=[[The News Tribune]] |access-date=July 22, 2019 |date=March 29, 2019}}</ref><ref name="joyce3">{{cite web |last1=Joyce |first1=Nathan |title=Federal Way's Jaden McDaniels named to Jordan Brand Classic all-star game |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/federal-ways-jaden-mcdaniels-named-to-jordan-brand-classic-all-star-game/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=July 22, 2019 |date=March 8, 2019}}</ref>

By the end of his high-school career, McDaniels was considered a consensus five-star recruit and the best [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] in the 2019 class.<ref name="247sports">{{cite web |title=Jaden McDaniels, Federal Way, Power Forward |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Jaden-McDaniels-46046881/high-school-200372/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=July 22, 2019}}</ref> [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] ranked him among the top 10 players in his class.<ref name="rivals">{{cite web |title=Jaden McDaniels, 2019 Power forward |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2019/jaden-mcdaniels-208389 |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |access-date=July 22, 2019}}</ref><ref name="espnrecruiting">{{cite web |title=Jaden McDaniels |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/234172/jaden-mcdaniels |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 22, 2019}}</ref> On May 22, 2019, McDaniels committed to play college basketball for [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]]. He had also received strong interest from [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] during the recruiting process.<ref name="commit">{{cite web |title=UW scores second top-7 recruit in PF McDaniels |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26798303/uw-scores-second-top-7-recruit-pf-mcdaniels |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 22, 2019 |date=May 22, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Jaden McDaniels.jpg|thumb|McDaniels (right) at the [[2019 Diamond Head Classic]]]]
Heading in to the college season, McDaniels was considered a possible number-one pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=2019-01-23 |title=2020 NBA mock draft: New No. 1 pick, latest on top prospects |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/insider/story/_/id/25826785/2020-nba-mock-draft-new-no-1-pick-scouting-lamelo-ball |access-date=2021-10-06 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> In his collegiate debut at Washington, a 67–64 upset win over [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], he scored 18 points and seven rebounds<ref>{{cite news |title=Washington rallies, stuns No. 16 Baylor 67-64 in Alaska |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169602 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111122537/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169602 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 11, 2020 |access-date=November 11, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 9, 2019}}</ref>. He finished the season with a high of 22 points against [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]]. As a freshman, McDaniels averaged 13 points and 5.8 rebounds per game while starting 21 games but began coming off the bench midway through conference play. After the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Washington freshman Jaden McDaniels declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29039539/washington-freshman-jaden-mcdaniels-declares-nba-draft |access-date=April 15, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 15, 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== Minnesota Timberwolves (2020–present) ===
In the [[2020 NBA draft]], the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] selected McDaniels in the first round with the 28th overall selection. He was then traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] along with [[Danny Green (basketball)|Danny Green]] for [[Dennis Schröder]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-acquire-dennis-schroder|title=Lakers Acquire Dennis Schröder|work=Lakers.com|date=November 18, 2020}}</ref> and later traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], along with the draft rights of [[Immanuel Quickley]], in exchange for [[Aleksej Pokuševski]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=November 20, 2020|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Ricky Rubio And Draft Rights To Jaden McDaniels From Oklahoma City And Draft Rights To Leandro Bolmaro From New York |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-ricky-rubio-and-draft-rights-jaden-mcdaniels-oklahoma-city-and|website=NBA.com|language=en-US}}</ref>

On December 27, 2020, McDaniels made his NBA debut recording 6 points and 1 rebound in 8 minutes off the bench in a 127-91 loss against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-12-28 |title=McDaniels Makes NBA Debut at Staples Center Against Lakers |url=https://www.si.com/college/washington/legends/mcdaniels-makes-nba-debut-at-staples-center-against-lakers |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=Washington Huskies On SI |language=en-US}}</ref>

On April 9, 2023, McDaniels sustained a fracture in his right hand after he punched a wall following a 113–108 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Timberwolves' Jaden McDaniels: Diagnosed with fractured hand|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/timberwolves-jaden-mcdaniels-diagnosed-with-fractured-hand/|access-date=2023-04-19|website=cbssports.com|date=April 9, 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

On October 23, 2023, McDaniels signed a five-year contract extension with the Timberwolves worth $136 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/wolves-jaden-mcdaniels-agree-to-extension-2023|title=Wolves, Jaden McDaniels agree to $136M contract extension|website=nba.com|date=October 23, 2023|access-date=October 24, 2023}}</ref> During an on-court altercation at a November 14 game between the Timberwolves and the [[Golden State Warriors]], McDaniels pulled [[Klay Thompson]] over and ripped his jersey, which started a brawl. Timberwolves center [[Rudy Gobert]] attempted to pull Thompson away from McDaniels, but [[Draymond Green]] put Gobert into a chokehold. McDaniels was ejected from the game and fined for the incident.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chen |first=Sonja |date=2023-11-15 |title=Draymond Green, Klay Thompson, Jaden McDaniels ejected after altercation |url=https://www.nba.com/news/timberwolves-warriors-ejections |access-date=2024-01-05 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-16 |title= Warriors' Draymond Green suspended five games for grabbing Rudy Gobert; three players fined  |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/warriors-draymond-green-suspended-five-games-for-grabbing-rudy-gobert-three-players-fined/article_5d8d4cbe-1b96-5e0f-904a-c20ebb885453.html |access-date=2023-11-16 |website=Toronto Star |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On April 23, 2024, McDaniels led all scorers with a playoff career-high 25 points in a 105–93 victory over the [[Phoenix Suns]] in Game 2 of the first round.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/timberwolves-jaden-mcdaniels-erupts-for-team-high-25-points/|title=Timberwolves' Jaden McDaniels: Erupts for team-high 25 points|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=April 24, 2024|access-date=April 26, 2024}}</ref> About a year before the playoff matchup, [[Anthony Edwards (basketball)|Anthony Edwards]] uttered how the Suns "got [[Kevin Durant|KD]], but we got Jaden McDaniels".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/timberwolves/jaden-mcdaniels-trash-talk-nuggets-playoff-stats|title=Jaden McDaniels Is the NBA’s New King of Trash Talk|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=May 1, 2026|access-date=June 26, 2026}}</ref> The Timberwolves went on to sweep the Suns and advance to the second round.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/game/min-vs-phx-0042300164?watchRecap=true | title=Minnesota Timberwolves vs Phoenix Suns Apr 28, 2024 Game Summary | website=[[NBA.com]] }}</ref>

McDaniels was named to the 2023-2024 [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-21 |title= Rudy Gobert, Victor Wembanyama headline 2023-24 Kia NBA All-Defensive teams|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-all-defensive-teams-announced |access-date=2024-05-21 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

The [[2024–25 NBA season|2024-25 season]] saw McDaniels begin to take an offensive leap, notching a career-high 30 points in a 114–98 victory against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on February 8, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 8, 2025 |title=McDaniels, Reid lead Edwards-less Timberwolves past Trail Blazers, 114-98 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705313 |access-date=July 18, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He was instrumental in the Timberwolves' historic 25-point comeback against the first-place [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on February 24, converting a [[three-point play]] to send the game to overtime. He led all Minnesota scorers with 27 points as the Timberwolves won 131–128 in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2025 |title=McDaniels scores 27, and Timberwolves rally from 25-point deficit to beat Thunder 131-128 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705392 |access-date=July 18, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> McDaniels started all 82 games for the Timberwolves during the season, posting averages of 12.2 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 2.0 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=11 NBA iron men who played all 82 games this season, including an old and tiny Chris Paul|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2025/4/14/24408190/nba-players-all-82-games-appear-ironman-chris-paul-mikal-bridges|access-date=July 19, 2025|website=sbnation.com|language=en}}</ref>

On April 25, 2025, McDaniels scored a then-playoff career-high 30 points in a 116–104 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in Game 3 of the first round.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 25, 2025 |title=Wolves top Lakers 116-104 in Game 3 to take series lead behind both-ways standout Jaden McDaniels |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401768056 |access-date=July 18, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> The Timberwolves later won the series 4–1 and advanced to the second round.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rhim |first=Kris |date=May 1, 2025 |title=Timberwolves eliminate Lakers behind Rudy Gobert's 27-24 game |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44944858/wolves-win-third-straight-eliminate-lakers-first-round |access-date=July 18, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On March 30, 2026, McDaniels was diagnosed with left knee [[patella]] [[tendinopathy]] and a bone bruise. He would not require surgery.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jaden McDaniels brutal injury update: Diagnosed with knee issue |url=https://basketnews.com/news-244094-jaden-mcdaniels-brutal-injury-update-diagnosed-with-knee-issue.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=15 April 2026 |language=en}}</ref> 

On April 30, 2026, in Game 6 of the first round, McDaniels scored a playoff career-high 32 points along with 10 rebounds in a 110–98 closeout victory over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Press |first=Associated |date=2026-05-01 |title=Jaden McDaniels leads Wolves on both ends as Nuggets ousted |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/48644115/jaden-mcdaniels-leads-wolves-ends-nuggets-ousted |access-date=2026-05-01 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
McDaniels's older brother, [[Jalen McDaniels]], played basketball for [[Federal Way High School]], where he was a four-star recruit,<ref name="ruiz">{{cite web |last1=Ruiz |first1=Drew |title=NBA-Bound Jalen and Jaden McDaniels are Pushing Each Other into the Next Gear |url=https://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/mcdaniels-feat/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |access-date=July 21, 2019 |date=October 22, 2018}}</ref> before joining the University of Washington at the college level. He was selected by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the second round of the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2019 Draft Prospect - Jalen McDaniels |url=https://www.nba.com/draft/2019/prospects/jalen-mcdaniels#/ |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |access-date=July 21, 2019}}</ref> McDanielsʼs mother is a cousin of former NBA player [[Juwan Howard]].<ref name=tj/> Both his father, Will McDaniels, and his mother, Angela Jackson, are originally from [[Chicago]].<ref name=evans2/>. In June of 2024, Jaden and his partner, Allison Audrey, welcomed his first son Mekhi.
